title: NLog
description: NLog is a flexible and high-performance logging library for .NET. It supports multiple targets (file, database, email, console) and allows configuration via XML or code.

data.text: NLog is a mature logging framework that makes it easy to write logs to many different destinations called targets. You can configure NLog using an XML file or entirely in code, giving you flexibility for both simple and complex scenarios.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the NLog core package and targets.
data.code:
dotnet add package NLog
dotnet add package NLog.Targets.Console
dotnet add package NLog.Targets.File

data.title: Basic NLog Setup
data.content: Configure NLog programmatically with console and file targets.

terms.definition: A destination where NLog writes log events, such as Console, File, Database, or Email.
The main object used to write log messages. Obtain one via LogManager.GetCurrentClassLogger().
The severity of a log event: Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, or Fatal.

data.title: XML Configuration
data.text: For production apps, you can move the configuration to NLog.config and use NLog.Extensions.Logging for seamless ASP.NET Core integration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NLog supports multiple targets out of the box
Configuration can be done in code or XML
Log levels let you filter messages by severity
data.takeaway: NLog is a flexible choice when you need logs in multiple places without changing your code.

data.title: Exercise: Configure NLog Targets
data.description: Set up NLog to write to both the console and a file.
steps: Install NLog and the Console and File targets
Configure two targets: console for Info+ and file for Debug+
Log messages at different levels (Debug, Info, Warn, Error)
Open the log file and verify both targets received the expected messages
data.expectedOutcome: Console shows Info and above, while the log file captures Debug and all higher-severity messages.
